caption: Figure E9-1, the free-space azimuth pattern three exam questions read. A full-circle polar plot with 0 degrees at the right, radial spokes every 15 degrees, and concentric dB rings labeled -3, -6, -12, and -24 stacked near the top; the outer circle is the 0 dB reference. The heavy trace is the antenna pattern: the main lobe centered on 0 degrees touches the outer ring and crosses the -3 dB ring at about plus and minus 25 degrees, so the 3 dB beamwidth is 2 x 25 = 50 degrees (E9B01). The rear lobe at 180 degrees sits at about -18 dB, so the front-to-back ratio is 18 dB (E9B02). The trace level at plus and minus 90 degrees is about -14 dB, so the front-to-side ratio is 14 dB (E9B03) - read the 90-degree value, not the -12 dB sidelobe level near plus and minus 55 degrees, which is the trap. Redrawn from the NCVEC pool figure.

spoken: A circular polar plot titled Figure E9-1, captioned Free-Space Pattern at the upper right. Zero degrees is at the right, 180 at the left, with spokes every 15 degrees; concentric rings are labeled minus 3, minus 6, minus 12, and minus 24 dB from outside in, and the outer circle is the 0 dB reference. A heavy trace shows the pattern: a large main lobe pointing right touches the outer ring and crosses the minus 3 dB ring at plus and minus 25 degrees - a 50 degree beamwidth. Small sidelobes sit near plus and minus 55 degrees at about minus 12 dB, deep nulls drop below minus 24 near plus and minus 75 degrees and flanking the rear, the trace reads about minus 14 dB straight up and down at 90 degrees, and the small rear lobe at 180 degrees sits at about minus 18 dB. Those three reads answer the three figure questions: 50 degrees, 18 dB front-to-back, 14 dB front-to-side.
